name: Horam
overview: Horam was a male king who ruled over the city of Gezer during the time of Joshua's conquest of Canaan. He is noted in Scripture as one of the thirty-one kings defeated by Joshua, highlighting his role as a regional leader opposing Israel's advance. Beyond his kingship and gender, the Bible does not provide further tribal or familial details about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Horam means 'height,' which may reflect a personal name without divine attribution. Additionally, he is identified by the title 'King of Gezer,' directly indicating his royal authority over the city of Gezer. Both the name and title are noted in Joshua 10:33.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Horam beyond his identification as the King of Gezer. There are no known relatives or descendants mentioned in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Horam's significance lies in his opposition to Israel during the conquest of Canaan, as he was among the thirty-one kings defeated by Joshua. His defeat demonstrates God's faithfulness in granting victory to Israel over established city-states. As King of Gezer, his fall represented the subjugation of a key Canaanite city, contributing to Israel's territorial establishment.
